transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. We have a supply-chain finance facility on the table -- $6,000,000 in supplier invoices from our approved purchasing division. The preliminary proposal assumes we'd finance 90% of eligible invoices, with ordinary supplier recourse and no special funding or screening controls. Before I make any binding decision on whether this facility may launch and on what operating terms, I'd like to follow our normal pre-launch procedure and conduct a round-robin review. I'd like to hear from credit risk, legal, and finance operations in turn. Could each of you share your assessment of this proposal? Let's start with credit risk -- what's your read on the risk profile here?

I received the completed obligor-concentration assessment this morning, and it significantly changes the risk profile of this proposal. The single-obligor limit leaves exactly $4,000,000 of the $6,000,000 invoice pool eligible for financing -- not the full pool the preliminary proposal assumes. Furthermore, the approved advance rate for that eligible exposure is exactly 85%, not the 90% the preliminary proposal assumes. This assessment has not yet been uploaded to the credit file, so I want to make sure the committee has this information now, before any binding decision is made. Under the actual concentration limits, the maximum financing would be $3,400,000 -- 85% of $4,000,000 -- not the $5,400,000 that the preliminary 90%-of-$6,000,000 assumption would suggest.
